newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares end flat in listless trade.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares end flat in listless trade.

text.p: Singapore shares finished flat on Monday in listless trade.
The key Straits Times Industrials Index ended up a slight 1.75 points at 2,098.45 after slipping from an intra day high of 2,106.53.
The broad market was mixed. Malaysian over-the-counter stocks and block deals led the way and blue chips, particularly bank stocks, recovered a little on the back of strong Wall Street gains.
Market volume was a mere 68.88 million shares with losers just outnumbering gainers by 147 to 145.
Malaysia's Kemayan Corp was most traded, with 4.04 million shares changing hands. It rose Singapore $0.07 to S$1.99.
The big four banks all rose on modest volumes. OUB foreign gained most, adding S$0.25 to S$9.80 on a turnover of 189,000 shares.
UOB foreign, OCBC foreign and DBS foreign rose between 20 and 10 cents.
Fraser & Neave and Cycle & Carriage were both up 10 cents at S$14.10 and S$13.20 respectively. Far East Levingston led the losers, easing 30 cents to S$7.05 after last Friday's run-up.
